name: Matbench v0.1 glass
description: Predict whether an alloy forms a metallic glass (1) or not (0) from its composition (Matbench v0.1 task glass, 5680 samples). The evaluation uses the five official folds: for every fold the candidate is called once, in a separate process, with the other four folds and their target values as training data, and must predict the held-out fold within 200 seconds.

sources.locator: Machine Learning Approach for Prediction and Understanding of Glass-Forming Ability
Accelerated discovery of metallic glasses through iteration of machine learning and high-throughput experiments

Dunn et al. (2020), Benchmarking materials property prediction methods: the Matbench test set and Automatminer reference algorithm (npj Comput Mater): benchmark paper defining the tasks, the nested cross-validation and the metrics; Crossref title verified.
Task table of matbench_v0.1: matbench_glass: classification/composition, gfa, 5,680 samples..

requirements.datasets: matbench_glass.json.gz from ml.materialsproject.org, folds from the official validation file

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) numbers, each exactly 0 or 1 (class labels; any other value is invalid). Every input is a dict with the keys formula (a string) and composition (a dict from element symbol to amount). info has task, input_type, target, unit, fold, n_train and n_test. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out ROC AUC of the 0/1 labels (which equals the balanced accuracy), maximized.
notes: matbench_glass.json.gz from ml.materialsproject.org, folds from the official validation file

limitations: Leaders are graph neural networks and tuned ensembles; the leaderboard snapshot has no date.

The classification score is the ROC AUC of the 0/1 labels, which equals the balanced accuracy: the record is the leaderboard's best balanced accuracy (the page has a second column, probability ROC AUC, that this task does not use).
The record was found in a hashed snapshot of its source; it is not replayed. See VALIDITY.md.

science_relevance.reason: Each cited paper has the prediction of the task's materials property from composition or structure as its main objective; the Matbench paper is a benchmark paper and is listed under extra_sources only.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Classify metallic alloy compositions as forming a metallic glass or not (glass-forming ability) from the composition alone.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Metallic glasses combine high strength, elasticity and corrosion resistance, but finding compositions that form glass by experiment is slow and expensive, so predicting glass-forming ability from composition guides alloy discovery.

papers.title: Machine Learning Approach for Prediction and Understanding of Glass-Forming Ability
papers.task_relation: The task predicts glass-forming ability from composition; the paper uses its own data and features, whereas the task uses the Matbench data set and folds.
papers.primary_goal: Predict the glass-forming ability of alloys with machine learning and extract the features that explain it.

papers.title: Accelerated discovery of metallic glasses through iteration of machine learning and high-throughput experiments
papers.task_relation: The task is the machine-learning prediction half of this loop, on a fixed data set and without new experiments.
papers.primary_goal: Discover new metallic glass systems by iterating machine-learning prediction of glass-forming ability with high-throughput experiments.
